title: Optimistic Output Harmonizer: routing, acceptance metrics, and staged fallback protocol
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement an experimental runtime component (the 'Optimistic Output Harmonizer') that (1) routes candidate speculative decoders based on kernel/latency profile and workload fingerprints, (2) computes a compact acceptance confidence metric per candidate, and (3) orchestrates a staged fallback that preserves SLOs when speculative outputs are rejected.

Why: Current speculative-decode prototypes focus on fast-path selection but lack a compact, runtime-native acceptance signal and an operational safe-retract path that protects tail latency and correctness. The Harmonizer is intended to be lightweight, pluggable into the runtime multiplexer, and to enable safe canarying of new speculative strategies without full rollout risk.

Scope:
- Routing: implement a rule-and-metrics driven router that picks up to N speculative decoders (N configurable per route) based on kernel affinity, recent tail-latency percentiles, and model variant cost multiplier.
- Acceptance metric: design a 3-field compact acceptance score (confidence, entropy-delta, kernel-fit) emitted alongside speculative outputs for quick decisions by the commit arbiter.
- Fallback protocol: staged retract sequence: soft-hold -> probe-commit -> full-retract. The runtime must support 'soft-hold' of tokens for up to X ms to allow acceptance to arrive.
- Telemetry: add per-decision telemetry points (router_choice, acceptance_score, decision_latency, fallback_reason).
- Safety: integrate with existing SLO guardrail to abort speculative flows if 95th latency or error-rate exceeds thresholds.

Non-goals: global model re-training, offline acceptance calibration infrastructure (only local online calibrator included in this task).

Deliverables:
1) Runtime patch to add Harmonizer shim and API endpoints for route selection.
2) Compact acceptance score protobuf and shaping rules.
3) Telemetry dashboards (Datadog links in attachments) and acceptance histograms.
4) PR with integration tests and a small canary rollout plan documented in the runbook.
comments: 2026-03-01: Ticket created by Aisha. Initial spec sketched after runtime sync. Raised question about soft-hold latency budget (suggested 8-12ms).

2026-03-03: Architecture review with runtime team. Decided on pluggable router interface rather than inline rewrite to minimize blast radius. Liam volunteered to prototype the acceptance score. Action: add telemetry hooks to prefill and decoder boundary. (Action-ENG-990001-A)

2026-03-05: Design feedback from PM (Ravi Kumar): ensure canary path allows partial traffic split by route tag and provides automatic rollback trigger based on 95th percentile latency. Added 'canary_route_tag' to plan.

2026-03-07: Implementer note: evaluated two candidate acceptance formulas. Chosen formula uses confidence + entropy-delta normalized by kernel-fit penalty. Running microbenchmarks shows median decision latency ~0.7ms added on top of speculative path.
2026-03-09: Safety review comments from Security (Marta Lee): require security_review_required for any route that evaluates customer prompt content against heuristics. Marking flag in ticket.
